summary: Comments on RFC 123 from MIT Project MAC. Requiring exactly 32 bits for the first connection is hard for some 36-bit machines such as their PDP-10. They suggest letting the server send more bits, filled with nulls, with an 8-bit byte size.

eli5.summary: A box that holds exactly 32 beads is awkward if your hands only grab 36. The writer asks for a slightly bigger box with empty space.

subtitle: A short complaint that the 32-bit initial connection rule is awkward for 36-bit machines.

tldr.problem: RFC 123 requires the byte size to be 32 bits for the initial connection, which strains some 36-bit machines.
tldr.mechanism: The author suggests letting the server send more than 32 bits, say 72, with the remaining bits as NULL fillers, and fixing the byte size at 8 bits.
tldr.outcome: It is a comment, not a specification, and the text does not say whether the change was adopted.

today: The unit metadata lists the status of RFC 148 as Unknown. It updates RFC 123 and has no obsoleting or updating RFCs.

sections.title: The Problem with a 32-Bit Initial Connection
sections.content:
A. Bhushan of MIT Project MAC comments on RFC 123. That RFC requires the byte size s to be 32 bits for the initial connection. The author says this puts severe strains on some of the 36-bit machines.

The example is their PDP-10 (DMCG-ITS) NCP, which has no way of sending or receiving exactly 32 bits of data at present.
sections.eli5: The rule asks for exactly 32 bits, but their computer can only handle data in bigger or different-sized pieces.

sections.title: Why It Is Hard and What Is Suggested
sections.content:
Their NCP transmits data either in image mode, which uses 36-bit bytes, or in ASCII mode, which uses 8-bit characters with the 8th bit as zero. Neither gives exactly 32 bits.

The suggestion is to permit the server to send more than 32 bits (say 72 bits), where the remaining bits could be NULL fillers. The byte size s for the connection may then be fixed at 8 bits.
sections.eli5: Let the sender use a bigger envelope and fill the extra room with blank paper, so machines with odd hand sizes can still play.

sections.title: Scope of the Comment
sections.content: The note is one short paragraph. It is phrased as a suggestion ("Perhaps we should permit...") and gives no formal protocol text. The RFC text does not record how the comment was received.
sections.eli5: It is a polite suggestion, not an order. Nobody wrote down here what happened next.

references.text: The RFC being commented on, RFC 123.
